findings.title: Embedded post author link uses wrong lightness pair
findings.body: The original rule used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) for light themes and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) for dark themes, so the embedded post author link becomes much lighter/lower-contrast on the light theme and darker on the dark theme. The intended complementary values are primary 30% and secondary 70%.

findings.title: Group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: This rule previously used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) for light themes, changing the intended text color instead of only adding a dark-theme alternative. It should use primary 30% and secondary 70%.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color changed from 30% to 50% lightness
findings.body: The original rule used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) for light themes, so mobile group member names lose the intended contrast. The correct complementary conversion is primary 30% and secondary 70%.

findings.title: Mobile topic map heading uses 50% instead of original 20% lightness
findings.body: The original h3 color for the mobile topic map was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%), making the heading noticeably lighter in light themes and changing the dark-theme result as well. It should be primary 20% and secondary 80%.

findings.title: Custom message length color inverts lightness values
findings.body: The original color was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The replacement uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) for light themes and scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) for dark themes, flipping the intended contrast in both themes. The correct complementary pair is primary 70% and secondary 30%.

findings.title: Category badge notification color was missed in dark-theme conversion
findings.body: This changed file still has .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification using scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) without a dark-light-choose() alternative. Dark themes will still derive this text color from $primary, so the same dark-theme contrast issue this PR addresses remains for category badge counts. It should use dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)).
